subject: Taxes
title: How Corporate Rates Have Fallen
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How Corporate Rates Have Fallen.

hook.text: In 1950, the US corporate tax rate was 42%. Today it's 21%.

buildup.text: The Reagan era began the decline: from 46% to 34% in 1986. Bush, Obama, and Trump each pushed further reductions.

discovery.text: The 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act slashed the rate from 35% to 21%—the largest corporate rate cut in US history.

twist.text: Globally, the average corporate rate fell from 40% in 1980 to 23% in 2023. It's a worldwide trend, not just American.

climax.text: As corporate rates fall, individual taxes and borrowing fill the gap. The shift is gradual but massive over decades.

punchline.text: 42% in 1950, 21% today. Corporations pay less; individuals pay more.

quiz.question: What was the US corporate tax rate before the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act?
